players.product: OlympusMAX dry / adiabatic coolers and Marley Everest cooling towers for data-center heat rejection

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 revenue increased 23% year-over-year with 17% organic growth; adjusted EBITDA grew 20% and adjusted EPS grew 22% to $2.02. HVAC segment revenue grew 27.6% (18.9% organic) with double-digit growth in both cooling and heating; HVAC segment margin declined 260 basis points on capacity-expansion startup costs and tariffs.

Data center revenue trajectory: approximately $150 million two years ago, $200 million last year, a plan for $300 million this year that was raised to $350 million last quarter and now to $430 million for the full year - growth of about 115%. Full-year adjusted EPS guidance raised by $0.45 to a midpoint of $8.40 on additional data center volume, D&M strength and the Neptronic acquisition; the midpoint implies 27% adjusted EBITDA growth.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 data center revenue $430 million (was $300 million plan, $350 million last quarter; $200 million in 2025); adj. EPS midpoint $8.40; 27% adj. EBITDA growth

quarterly_data.signal: Total data center capacity once at full production is now expected to be approximately $1.1 billion, up from the prior expectation of approximately $750 million, because OlympusMAX throughput in Olathe and Springfield exceeded initial expectations after lean, productivity and flow-optimization work, and the core Everest cooling-tower business gained space and staffing. Full production capacity is expected in the second half of 2028, with a bias that it could be earlier.
quarterly_data.figure: data center capacity ~$1.1 billion at full production (prior ~$750 million); full production 2H 2028

quarterly_data.signal: HVAC segment backlog at quarter end was $919 million, up 59% organically year-over-year, primarily driven by strong data center demand; HVAC book-to-bill was about 1.4x. Only formal purchase orders go into backlog - long-term agreements with several customers (mainly hyperscalers) sit outside it.
quarterly_data.figure: HVAC backlog $919 million (+59% organic YoY); HVAC book-to-bill ~1.4x

quarterly_data.signal: In July SPX launched assembly of the OlympusMAX at its new Madison, Alabama facility and will add production capabilities there during the first half of 2027; Tamco's new Tennessee facility for engineered aluminum dampers is on track for full production in 2027. OlympusMAX is built in both Olathe (core cooling plant) and Madison.
quarterly_data.figure: Madison, Alabama OlympusMAX assembly started July 2026; production capabilities 1H 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Market shift toward SPX solutions: as more liquid cooling goes under the roof, dry cooling appears to be the most favored heat-rejection solution, with adiabatic and cooling towers also in demand; SPX sees significantly increasing demand from existing hyperscalers and had nice wins with colos and neoclouds. Hyperscalers give visibility several years forward because they need SPX's product to turn the data center on and send teams of 10 people into SPX facilities for two weeks at a time.

Supply chain: SPX engineers its own fans, gear reducers and heat exchangers, giving it flexibility to build in-house or use third parties; before taking any large data-center order its supply chain team scrubs every bill-of-material item to validate it can deliver, having watched competitors fall down on supply chain. Management notes some customer concentration among a small number of hyperscalers.

2026 CapEx guidance of $135 million-$165 million, back-half weighted, covers the plant expansions (some could slip into 2027); regular-way CapEx is 1.5%-2% of revenue. Data center incrementals are expected to match the rest of HVAC at high 20% to low 30% segment-margin incrementals. Neptronic acquisition (controls, electric duct heaters, humidification) adds ~$75 million of annual revenue at low-40% segment income margins, paid at about 12.5x, with data center exposure similar to or a tad higher than the HVAC segment's.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 CapEx $135 million-$165 million; incrementals high 20% to low 30%; Neptronic ~$75 million revenue at 12.5x
